title: Swas NDE 5243
content: Around 4:00 p.m. on November 15, 1984, with high rheumatic fever, I was standing by my bedroom window. After standing for a while, I felt my toes and the palms of my hands were getting numb, so I sat at the base of the window (the old houses in Kolkata will always have some place to sit at the base of the window, but if you choose to sit you cannot get much view of the outside). I pinched my toes but couldn't sense a thing. I also felt a sheer pain around my chest area at the same time. I could see my nanny sleeping on the marble floor. I tried to call her and wake her up, but she didn't answer. I tried desperately to stand on my feet to get rid of that irritating numbness, and as I did I felt somebody snatch my soul from my body and start to fly me like a kite in the sky. There were several vertical iron rods placed in equal distance from one another in the window (this used to be a common structure in old construction houses). My soul flew from the space in between two of those rods. I felt like a bird. I immediately looked back and saw my pale and fragile frame, lying at the base of the window with eyes closed, saliva dripping out of the wide-open mouth and a skeletal right hand that was somehow entangled with one of the rods. I was shocked, but didn't realize I was dead. I then flew above the row of houses in that area. I saw children playing in the park, telegraph poles, television antennas on the roof of our neighbor's houses and wet clothes hanging on the balcony. As I flew more, I began to see unfamiliar faces shouting from the streets, young men discussing a cricket match. Suddenly the city view started fading away and somebody pushed me into a pitch-black space. When that black space arrived, I started flying even faster. I was really scared as I couldn't see a thing, but could strongly feel that somebody was pulling a thread, at the end of which my soul was lying. After a while, I saw a thousand suns but felt no heat - it was a bit cold for my preference. My eyes were not blurred by the sunshine, neither were my senses. I was wondering why it was not so hot in spite of so much of sunshine - I still keep on thinking about this. Next, I was hit against a rock like structure but wasn't hurt, and immediately started flying back to the direction where I started my journey form. I flew back to me with a speed double to what I started from. When I was about to enter my body I heard one of the nurses frantically saying that I had no pulse. The doctor saw me at 4:45 p.m.

out_of_body.vantage_other_detail: Flew out through the space between vertical iron rods in the bedroom window and then above a row of houses/city streets.
out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: Felt 'somebody snatch my soul from my body and start to fly me like a kite in the sky.'

tunnel.movement_other_detail: Felt 'somebody was pulling a thread, at the end of which my soul was lying.'

arrival.other_being_detail: Unseen presence that 'pushed me into a pitch-black space' and seemed to be pulling a 'thread.'

environment.environment_other_detail: Cityscape details (houses, park, telegraph poles, TV antennas, wet clothes on balcony); later a 'pitch-black space'; later 'a thousand suns' and a 'rock like structure'.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: High rheumatic fever; chest pain; numbness; later a nurse said there was no pulse.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Dark void/black space; intense light described as 'a thousand suns'; impact with rock-like structure; auditory perception of nurse saying 'no pulse.'
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE over body and city, then pushed into black space (void), then intense light ('a thousand suns'), then rapid return to body.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Soul described as being flown 'like a kite' with an unseen being pulling a 'thread'; exited through window iron rods; 'hit against a rock like structure' without pain; 'a thousand suns' with no heat and feeling cold.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I felt somebody snatch my soul from my body and start to fly me like a kite in the sky.” “Somebody pushed me into a pitch-black space.” “I saw a thousand suns but felt no heat - it was a bit cold for my preference.” “I heard one of the nurses frantically saying that I had no pulse.”
